info.name: PDF Knowledge Assistant
info.description: Endpoints for pdf-knowledge-assistant: chat, RAG chat, and directory-based document ingestion.

request.description: Plain chat with the LLM, no retrieval augmentation.

Chat augmented with similarity search results from the vector store. Response is JSON: {"answer": "...", "sources": [{"file": "...", "page": 1, "path": "/abs/path/to/file.pdf"}, ...]}. "path" is the file's real absolute location on disk.

query.description: Absolute directory to list. Omit (or leave blank) to list the home directory.
List filesystem roots instead (drive letters on Windows, / on macOS/Linux). Disable this query param to use 'path' instead.

request.description: Lists a directory's subfolders using plain java.nio.file calls — no OS dialog, no AWT. Omit 'path' to list the home directory, or enable the 'roots' query param to list filesystem roots (drive letters on Windows, / on macOS/Linux) instead. Each entry includes 'pdfCount', a non-recursive count of PDFs directly inside it. The UI's 'Browse Folder…' button drives this endpoint to render an in-app folder browser; 'Ingest Directory' below then does the actual ingestion once you've picked a folder.

Scans 'directory' on disk for PDFs and adds them to the vector store, reading each file in place (nothing is copied or uploaded). 'recursive' defaults to true when omitted. Each chunk's metadata records the file's real absolute path, which /chat/rag returns in its 'sources'. The UI normally gets 'directory' from the in-app folder browser ('Browse Directory' above) rather than the user typing it, but this endpoint works standalone too.

query.description: Absolute path to an already-ingested .pdf file, as returned in a /chat/rag source's 'path' field.

request.description: Streams the PDF at 'path' straight off disk (Content-Type: application/pdf, Content-Disposition: inline) so it can be opened directly — nothing is copied. This is what each clickable citation in the UI links to, with a '#page=N' fragment appended client-side to jump to the cited page. Trusts any existing, readable .pdf path it's given; fine for a personal, localhost-only tool, not something to expose beyond that without adding access checks.
